_comment: STARTER PRESETS - order-of-magnitude values, NOT measured data.
They were assembled from typical ranges reported for the Kawabata Evaluation System (KES-F) and common textile-science conversions, then rounded:
tensile stiffness  k  ~ 2*WT/e^2 from KES tensile energy (N/m)
shear stiffness    G  from KES shear rigidity, 1 gf/(cm*deg) = 56.2 N/m/rad
bending rigidity   B  from KES bending, 1 gf*cm^2/cm = 9.81e-5 N*m
Real fabrics vary by 2-5x within one category (weave density, finish, yarn). Calibrate against a cantilever / Cusick drape test of your own cloth (see docs/ARCHITECTURE.md).
warp = along selvedge / wales, weft = across / courses.

fabrics.name: Cotton poplin (shirting)
fabrics.notes: ~120 g/m2 plain weave. Crisp but light.

fabrics.name: Cotton crepe
fabrics.notes: ~130 g/m2 plain weave with high-twist crepe yarns. Crinkled surface: softer and more fluid than poplin at the same weight, stretchier across the grain (crimp straightens first), matte with some spring.

fabrics.name: Denim 12 oz
fabrics.notes: ~400 g/m2 3x1 twill. Heavy, stiff, higher shear resistance.

fabrics.name: Linen (medium weight)
fabrics.notes: ~180 g/m2 plain weave. Stiffer and springier than cotton poplin at the same weight.

fabrics.name: Wool suiting (worsted)
fabrics.notes: ~250 g/m2 twill. Drapes well, shear-compliant (can be eased/shaped).

fabrics.name: Silk charmeuse
fabrics.notes: ~70 g/m2 satin weave. Very fluid, slippery.

fabrics.name: Polyester chiffon
fabrics.notes: ~40 g/m2 sheer plain weave. Extreme-light end of the range.

fabrics.name: Cotton single jersey (knit)
fabrics.notes: ~150 g/m2. Warp = wales (stiffer), weft = courses (stretchier). Very low shear stiffness, buckles easily under compression.

fabrics.name: Lambskin garment leather
fabrics.notes: ~0.7 mm. Isotropic, thick, resists shear and bending far more than fabrics of similar weight. Real leather also creeps and has a non-linear toe region that is not modelled yet.
